content: Let F be a group containing a finite index subgroup G that is a free discrete group of finite rank or the fundamental group of a compact orientable topological surface of genus ≥ 2, and H ⊆ F an infinite subgroup. Regard H, G ⊆ F ⊆ F̂ (F is residually finite), F̂ the profinite completion. Let γ ∈ F̂ with γ·H·γ^{-1} ⊆ F. Write H_G = H ∩ G. Then γ ∈ F·N_F̂(H_G), that is, γ·H_G·γ^{-1} = δ·H_G·δ^{-1} for some δ ∈ F. If moreover H_G is nonabelian, then γ ∈ F.

conclusion: (i) two-generated subgroups are free; (ii) separation of x ≠ 1 in the abelianization of a finite index subgroup; (iii) x^n, y^n span a rank two free abelian subgroup of G_1^ab; (iv) abelian subgroups are cyclic; (v) T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ; (vi) Z_Ĝ(N̂) = {1}; (vii) α = id.
content: Let G be as in Theorem 2.6 (free of finite rank, or an orientable surface group of genus ≥ 2) and Ĝ its profinite completion. (i) Any subgroup of G generated by two elements is free. (ii) For x ∈ G, x ≠ 1, there is a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G with x ∈ G_1 and x of nontrivial image in G_1^ab. (iii) For noncommuting x, y ∈ G there are a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G and n ≥ 1 with x^n, y^n ∈ G_1 whose images in G_1^ab generate a free abelian subgroup of rank two. (iv) Every abelian subgroup of G is cyclic. (v) If T̂ ⊆ Ĝ is a closed subgroup and there is a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing an isomorphism T̂ ≅ Ẑ, then T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ. (vi) If G is nonabelian and N̂ = Ker(Ĝ ↠ Ĝ^ab), the centralizer Z_Ĝ(N̂) is trivial. (vii) In the notation of (vi), an automorphism of the profinite group Ĝ that preserves N̂ and restricts to the identity on N̂ is the identity.
explicit_hypotheses: G a free discrete group of finite rank or the fundamental group of a compact orientable surface of genus ≥ 2 (as in Theorem 2.6)
Ĝ the profinite completion of G
(v): T̂ ⊆ Ĝ closed, with a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing T̂ ≅ Ẑ
(vi), (vii): G nonabelian; (vii): α an automorphism of Ĝ preserving N̂ with α|_N̂ = id
obligations: Several parts are classical facts whose Mathlib coverage was not checked; surface groups are not defined in Mathlib.

A witness needs a number field F containing √−1 and the full 6-torsion of E_F (hence, by the Weil pairing, a primitive cube root of unity, so F ⊇ Q(ζ_12); in particular F = Q(i) is impossible), semistable reduction of E_F at all finite places, a nonempty odd set S of places of k with multiplicative reduction above S, F/k Galois of degree prime to l, and a prime l ≥ 5 prime to the residue characteristics of S. See docs/INITIAL_THETA_DATA.md for a construction outline; no specific curve has been checked.

conclusion: Interpretation of the diagram of Corollary 3.6 (ii): Kummer, Galois evaluation and forgetting as in Fig. 3.1; the complementary roles of etale-like and Frobenius-like structures; the modified Theta-link qq_v -> {qq_v^{j^2}}_{1<=j<=l*} as a homotopy between the identity and qq_v -> qq_v^{(l*)^2}; Grothendieck Conjecture-type results as comparison isomorphisms.
content: On the diagram in the third display of Corollary 3.6 (ii), summarized as Fig. 3.1 (Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids => group-theoretic theta monoids via Kummer, Galois evaluation down to group-theoretic Gaussian monoids, and 'forget' back to Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian monoids). (i) The three portions correspond to Kummer, Galois evaluation and forgetting; forgetting yields post-anabelian monoids; the composite of Kummer and evaluation is a comparison isomorphism between Frobenius-like and etale-like structures, as in classical Hodge-Arakelov theory where the comparison isomorphism comes from evaluating theta functions and their derivatives at torsion points. (ii) Etale-like structures (etale or tempered fundamental groups) are invariant under non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters such as the Theta-link and the log-wall and are rigid via anabelian algorithms; Frobenius-like structures (abstract monoids) are not so rigidified, which allows such filters to be constructed; the two play complementary roles with respect to binding to conventional scheme theory (Fig. 3.2), and Kummer theory relates them within a Hodge theater. (iii) Composing the Theta-link qq_v -> Theta_v with the arrows of Fig. 3.1 gives the correspondence qq_v -> {qq_v^{j^2}}_{1<=j<=l*}, a 'modified Theta-link', viewed as an abstract combinatorial Frobenius lifting, a homotopy between the identity qq_v -> qq_v and qq_v -> qq_v^{(l*)^2}; the exponents {j^2} are highly distinguished (Remark 2.6.3). (iv) Grothendieck Conjecture-type results in anabelian geometry are comparison isomorphisms between polynomial-function-theoretic and group-theoretic collections of morphisms, obtained by combining considerations particular to the situation with Galois evaluation via Kummer theory of polynomial functions or differential forms at rational points.
obligations: Interpretive; no mathematical claim beyond Corollary 3.6 and the cited results. The objects (Theta-link, Gaussian monoids) have no Lean vocabulary.

content: F_l^{x+-} versus F_l*-symmetry: F_l approximates Z; F_l^{x+-} corresponds to addition, involves the zero label and units, and is applied for conjugate synchronization (uniradial, but coric after mono-analyticization); F_l* corresponds to multiplication, separates the zero label, describes the Gaussian monoids as functions of j in F_l*, and is multiradial. Volumes at each j in F_l* are given weight 1/l* so that the diagonal constant distribution has weight 1.

For an n-capsule {α𝔉}_{α∈A} of F-prime-strips and v | v_Q, log(αF_v) is an inductive limit of topological modules of finite dimension over Q_{v_Q}; the 1-tensor packet is v_Q ↦ log(αF_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{v|v_Q} log(αF_v), and the n-tensor packet is log(AF_{v_Q}) = ⊗_{α∈A} log(αF_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{{v_α}} {⊗_α log(αF_{v_α})}, tensor products of ind-topological modules (page 92). (i) The ind-topological field structures on the log(αF_v) determine an ind-topological ring structure on log(AF_{v_Q}), an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields; the decompositions are determined by the ring structure and compatible with the action of αΠ_v. (ii) For α ∈ A, v | v_Q: log(A,αF_v) = log(αF_v) ⊗ {⊗_{β∈A∖{α}} log(βF_{v_Q})} ⊆ log(AF_{v_Q}) is a direct summand and an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields. Tensoring with 1's in the factors β ≠ α gives a natural injective ring homomorphism log(αF_v) → log(A,αF_v) which, for suitable cofinal objects of the inductive systems, induces an isomorphism of an object of the domain onto each direct summand field of the corresponding object of the codomain. Hence the integral structure Ψ̄ = Ψ_{log(αF_v)} ∪ {0} ⊆ log(αF_v) determines integral structures on each direct summand field of log(A,αF_v) and log(AF_{v_Q}) (page 93). Remark 3.1.1 (i) (page 94): log(αF_v) ≅ k̄, Ψ̄ ≅ O_k̄, log(A,αF_v) ≅ ⊗ k̄ ≅ lim ⊕ k̄ ⊇ lim ⊕ O_k̄, so the integral structures are copies of O_k̄ in the copies of k̄.

Record two lattices and the map between them. Lattice L1 (the one on page 93): the product, over the direct summand fields of a finite object of log(A,αF_v) or log(AF_{v_Q}), of the copy of the ring of integers transported from Ψ̄ by the isomorphism of page 93; this is the normalization (integral closure) in the product of fields. Lattice L2 (not on page 93): the image of the tensor product of the rings of integers of the factors. The map is the inclusion L2 → L1 induced by the inclusions of rings of integers. Assessment, not from the page: L2 can be a proper order in L1, so the two must not be identified. Every later use (log-volume 0 of the integral structures, Prop 3.9 (i)) refers to L1.
Prove that the integral structure transported to a summand field does not depend on the cofinal object chosen.

content: (i) Concrete description of Prop 3.1: log(αF_v) ≅ k̄ with k = K_v, Ψ̄ ≅ O_k̄; integral structures are copies of O_k̄ (pages 93 to 94). (ii) Weights: log-volumes on the portion of log(αF_v) for K_v are taken with weight [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1}; for direct sums over v | v_Q the normalized weight is 1/([K_v:(F_mod)_v]·Σ_{w|v_Q}[(F_mod)_w : Q_{v_Q}]); for tensor products over α ∈ A the weight 1/∏_α[K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}], normalized to 1/((∏_α[K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}])·Σ_{{w_α}}∏_α[(F_mod)_{w_α}:Q_{v_Q}]); all normalized so that multiplication by p_{v_Q} adds or subtracts log(p_{v_Q}) (pages 94 to 95). content: A topological pseudo-monoid is a topological space P with a continuous map S → P, S ⊆ P × P, such that there are a topological abelian group M (written multiplicatively) and an embedding ι : P ↪ M with S = {(a, b) | ι(a)·ι(b) ∈ ι(P)} and S → P the restriction of the group law. With M discrete, P is a pseudo-monoid. P is divisible if M, ι can be chosen so that every element of M has n-th roots for all n ≥ 1 and a ∈ ι(P) if and only if a^n ∈ ι(P); P is cyclotomic if M, ι can be chosen with μ_M ≅ Q/Z, μ_M ⊆ ι(P) and μ_M·ι(P) ⊆ ι(P).

conclusion: Definition (no proof obligation).
content: For a topological group Π, B^temp(Π) is the category of countable discrete sets with continuous Π-action and Π-equivariant maps. Π is tempered if it is an inverse limit of an inverse system of surjections of countable discrete topological groups. A category equivalent to B^temp(Π) with Π tempered is a connected temperoid; then C ≃ (C^0)^⊤. For Galois-countable Π, Π is reconstructed up to inner automorphism from B^temp(Π) or B^temp(Π)^0, which defines π_1(C), π_1(C^0) for a Galois-countable connected temperoid C.
obligations: Tempered groups and temperoids are not in Mathlib; the reconstruction of π_1 cites Remark 2.5.3 (i), (T1), (T5).

For Galois-countable tempered Π_1, Π_2 there are natural bijections between continuous outer homomorphisms Π_1 → Π_2, morphisms B^temp(Π_1) → B^temp(Π_2), and morphisms B^temp(Π_1)^0 → B^temp(Π_2)^0.

content: To apply bi-coricity of units, one must use units vertically once-shifted, at (n,m−1), relative to the value group structures at (n,m) (Rem 3.11.3 (ii)). The conflict between needing a vertical shift and the impossibility of shifting (Step iii) is resolved by working on the 0-column with structures invariant under vertical shifts, namely vertically coric structures (n,◦), related to Frobenius-like structures by the log-Kummer correspondence of Thm 3.11 (ii), at the cost of the upper semi-compatibility Ind3.
obligations: Formalize the passage from Frobenius-like data at (0,0) to vertically coric data at (0,◦) and quantify the loss as a containment.

content: The copies of F_mod (global Frobenioids F_MOD, F_mod and realifications) bridge multiplicative global realified Frobenioids and their additive representations in mono-analytic log-shells; F_MOD is precisely compatible with the log-Kummer correspondence, hence suited to the link; F_mod is only upper semi-compatible (Ind3), hence suited to explicit degree estimates via log-volumes (Rem 3.10.1 (ii), (iii)).
